"'''The Imperial March''',"<ref name="SWG">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref> also referred to as the '''Martial Theme of the Empire''', was played across [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] territory during its [[Imperial Era/Legends|reign]]. It was most notably known as the martial theme of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], where the piece was often played during graduation ceremonies.<ref name="The Paradise Snare">''[[The Paradise Snare]]''</ref> A [[Jizz/Legends|jizz]] variation also existed.<ref name="Star Wars: Republic Commando">''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]''</ref>

==History==
The melody of the Imperial March was known to former [[Padawan/Legends|Jedi Padawan]] [[Ashara Zavros]] by around [[3640 BBY]].<ref name="TOR" /> The young [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] also briefly hummed the melody when he had completed a podrace.<ref name="Racer">[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Racer'']]</ref> The March's melody also appeared throughout the Clone Wars both as elevator music<ref name="Star Wars: Republic Commando" /> and a tune hummed by a [[Rocket battle droid/Legends|rocket battle droid]] when he and his party were intercepting [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon's]] escape pod.<ref name="Rising Malevolence">{{TCW|Rising Malevolence|Rising ''Malevolence''}}</ref> Later, the melody entered the use of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] as "The Imperial March," where, as its nickname implied, acted as the martial theme for their [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]].<ref name="The Paradise Snare" /> As such, members of the [[Stormtrooper Corps/Legends|Stormtrooper Corps]] and other Imperial personnel frequently hummed the musical piece during their battlefield operations.<ref name="Star Wars: Battlefront II">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref> Because of its stance as the martial theme of the Imperial Navy, it played during various graduation ceremonies for the organization, including that of Imperial Navy cadet [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] in [[10 BBY/Legends|10 BBY]],<ref name="The Paradise Snare" /> as well as in recruitment and propaganda films, such as one [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] watched during the events of the [[First Battle of Tatooine]].<ref name="NPR New Hope">[[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio drama]]</ref> In the aftermath of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], several musicians occasionally played the piece, as well as at least [[Darth Vader statuette|one]] [[Statuary|statuette]] playing the piece whenever someone approached 12 meters of distance from it.<ref name="SWG" /> In [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]], the Imperial researcher [[Leonis Murthé]] hummed this piece when attempting to cut up via [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] one of his "patients," a member of the [[Gulmarid]] species that were tortured by him.<ref name="Boba Fett: Agent of Doom">''[[Boba Fett: Agent of Doom]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Known as "'''The Imperial March'''" [[In-universe|out-of-universe]], the musical theme was used in both the films (barring ''A New Hope'') and the Expanded Universe of the ''Star Wars'' saga. Although it was normally an out-of-universe piece (see [[The Imperial March|main article]]), there have been instances in the Expanded Universe where it was used as an in-universe music piece, most notably in [[A. C. Crispin]]'s book ''[[The Paradise Snare]]''. Although it was never given an in-universe name in this instance, Han Solo and the narration did refer to it as the martial theme of the Empire during the graduation ceremony.

In ''Star Wars: Galaxies'', the Imperial March is playable via jukeboxes, although it is unknown whether it was a true in-universe piece due to it also playing out-of-universe pieces such as the Star Wars Main Theme. Similarly, it was also referred to in-universe as ''the Imperial March'' by musician classes and in the description of the Darth Vader statuette in ''Star Wars Galaxies''.
